# Render-surfaced source mismatches — product realty (difficulty real_estate_closing_plans)
Source: final report of the realty render agent (round 1, 2026-10-12), copied verbatim by the coordinator. Items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 are extended-source items routed to rework; item 4 is base-vs-base (BLUEPRINT-KNOWN, base frozen).

1. **Overwrite with unclear scope (`realty_ext_reissued_plan_invoice` on `realty_order_requirements`).** The retired clause is "The plan ordered may be changed to another plan at any time before closing, and the invoice is then reissued at the new plan's premium." Its replacement only covers the invoiced amount. It doesn't say whether the right to change plans "at any time before closing" survives. Because the whole sentence is now marked retired, the KB states that right only in the narrower rule that the buyer's agent may change the plan on a listing order before closing.
2. **Overwrite drops part of the clause (`realty_ext_buyer_direct_prepayment` on `realty_cancellation_and_credits`).** The retired clause includes "(escrow refunds go to the buyer once the escrow file is closed)". The replacement keeps "every other credit balance remains refunded within refund_processing_days calendar days to the party that paid the invoice" but leaves out the escrow-to-buyer parenthetical. Its status is now unstated.
3. **Overwrite drops part of the clause (`realty_ext_buyer_direct_prepayment` on `realty_premium_pricing`).** The retired clause "…is invoiced once per order, payable through escrow at closing" is replaced by text that doesn't mention "invoiced once per order".
4. **Base rule and formula disagree (`realty_cancellation_and_credits`).** The rule deducts "the benefit Bridgewell paid in the buyer phase", but the formula subtracts `realty_msr_contract_year_benefit_paid`, which counts the current contract year only. The two give different results on the Two-Year and Three-Year plans after the first year. The KB renders the rule text.
5. **Possible undeclared conflict.** Base `realty_premium_pricing` says "The invoice is due on the closing date". The extended reissue rule says the reissued invoice "is due on the expected closing date shown on the order", and the reissue tool body sets the due date from `expected_closing_date`. No overwrite covers this.
6. **Low severity.** The docstrings of both card tools (`pay_failed_sale_charge_by_card_a1a6aa51` and `prepay_plan_invoice_by_card_13fdf553`) say the payment uses "the payment card on your Bridgewell profile" and is "charged to the card exactly as given". The tool bodies only post a payment record with method card and read no card or profile.
